title: Diagnose your own work
opening: A message exists as a draft, but no message has arrived. Trace the work from the last event that happened to the next one that did not. The right repair depends on where the work stopped.

labels.diagnosisIntro: Choose a distinction to inspect. These questions help locate a break; they do not establish anyone’s motive.
labels.capacity: What may be missing at this transition?
labels.traceIntro: Record observable events in order. A plan or completion label is not proof that an event occurred.
labels.lastEvent: What is the last operation that actually happened?
labels.nextEvent: What was the next operation that did not happen?
labels.checkOutcome: What outcome will you inspect after the correction?
labels.private: This optional note is private practice. The six required course questions are separate.
labels.practiceIntro: Use observable events. Choose a possible break, make a correction at that transition, then inspect the outcome again.
labels.sampleLoaded: Illustration loaded. It is not a report of an observed outcome.
labels.length: This full note is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote: Choose one outcome that has stalled. Find the last operation that actually happened and the next one that did not. Then use the capacity table to locate the failure. Do you lack the ability, or have you avoided beginning? Did the work die when someone else took over? Are you repeating the same ineffective move? Did you fail to anticipate the next obstacle? Have you saved a lesson without using it? Make the correction at that point. Then inspect the outcome again. The plan exists. Did reality change?
labels.decision: The distinction is selected for inspection. It is not a conclusion about why the work stopped.

distinctions.title: Agency
distinctions.detail: Check whether the person or system had the ability needed for this operation.

distinctions.title: Initiative
distinctions.detail: Check whether the work began when it could have begun.

distinctions.title: Continuity
distinctions.detail: Check whether the work continued when someone else took over or an interruption happened.

distinctions.title: Durability
distinctions.detail: Check whether the result remained usable after the original maker moved on.

distinctions.title: Reliability
distinctions.detail: Check whether the operation happened consistently when needed.

distinctions.title: Effectiveness
distinctions.detail: Check whether the operation produced the intended result.

distinctions.title: Adaptation
distinctions.detail: Check whether the work changed when conditions changed.

distinctions.title: Prediction
distinctions.detail: Check whether a likely next obstacle was anticipated.

distinctions.title: Reuse and learning
distinctions.detail: Check whether a saved finding changed a later attempt.

steps.title: Find the last real event
steps.detail: Record what happened and the evidence that shows it.

steps.title: Name the next event that did not happen
steps.detail: Describe the missing operation without guessing at motive.

steps.title: Correct that transition
steps.detail: Choose a repair that fits the distinction you inspected.

steps.title: Inspect the outcome again
steps.detail: Check whether reality changed; if the outcome is still absent, inspect the next break or revise the diagnosis.

fields.label: What is the last operation that actually happened?
What was the next operation that did not happen?
Which capacity distinction will you inspect, and what evidence would help?
What correction fits that transition, and what outcome will you inspect afterward?

example.outcome: A message should reach its recipient.
example.last: The message was saved as a draft.
example.next: No authorized send occurred, so the recipient has not received it.
example.distinction: First check whether sending requires approval. If approval is missing, the next action needs that decision; if sending was authorized but skipped, inspect the execution step.
example.correction: Resolve any required approval or complete the authorized send, then inspect delivery evidence.

source.assessmentBoundary: Six required open-ended course questions remain separate from this optional private note. No qualified semantic grade or learner outcome is supplied.
